candidates.title: GCC 16.1 released: C++26 reflection / contracts / safety hardening, C++20 by default, and more!
candidates.summary: GCC 16.1 has been released! Lots of good C++26 material including reflection and contracts. GCC 16 Release Series: Changes, New Features, and Fixes From the announcement: C++20 by default: [...]  N.B. C++20 modules support is still experimental and must be enabled by  -fmodules . Several C++26 features have been implemented: P2996R13 , Reflection ( PR120775 , enabled by  -std=c++26 -freflection ) P3394R4 , Annotations for Reflection P3293R3 , Splicing a base class subobject P3096R
candidates.relevance_reason: This release of GCC brings C++26 features like reflection and contracts, which can improve C++ code quality, maintainability, and potentially performance in native Camera HAL implementations. It's a fallback for C++ relevance.
